title: A legal, honest label, and proof that your packaging works
course_title: Product Packaging & Branding for Small Producers

say: A legal, honest label, and proof that your packaging works.
This is the video for Module 3 of Product Packaging and Branding.

NAFDAC regulates processed food, drinks and cosmetics. To sell through shops and supermarkets, you need registration and a label that meets its rules. Always check the current guidelines for your product.

panel.heading: Quick label compliance check
items: Dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and a batch number

say: Your label needs the product name on the front, and the ingredients from largest to smallest, with allergens like groundnuts named clearly.

panel.heading: Quick label compliance check
items: Dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and a batch number

say: Net content in metric units, such as 300 g. And your business name and full address, not just a phone number.

panel.heading: Quick label compliance check
items: Dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and a batch number

say: Dates written day, month, full year, with a batch number, so each production run can be traced. And your NAFDAC number, exactly as issued.
If any box is unticked, the label is not ready for shops.

panel.heading: Quick label compliance check
items: Dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and a batch number

say: For example, Chika in Enugu wants a supermarket to stock her pepper sauce. Her label says Exp 12/26, has no weight, and only a phone number.
She writes Date of Manufacture and Best Before with the full year, adds net weight 300 g on the front, lists her ingredients, and prints her full address.
She has no NAFDAC number yet, so she does not print one. She starts registration instead.
Never print a NAFDAC number you have not been issued. A made-up, borrowed or expected number can lead to seizure of your goods and prosecution.

cards.d: A made-up or borrowed number is against the law and can lead to seizure and prosecution.
Never say a food or cream cures, treats or prevents a disease without approval.
Borrowing a famous product's look misleads buyers and can bring legal action.

say: Never make medical claims. For example, Hauwa's first shea butter label said cures eczema. She removed it completely.

cards.d: A made-up or borrowed number is against the law and can lead to seizure and prosecution.

say: And never copy the colours, layout or name style of a famous product. Build your own look, then protect it with CAC registration and a trademark.

say: Every claim must be true and something you could prove. Hauwa had no organic certificate, so organic came off. Chemical-free is never true, because water and salt are chemicals. And best in Africa cannot be proven.
She replaced them with honest, specific words: no added fragrance, which is true, and hand-whipped in Kaduna from unrefined shea butter. Her label is shorter, honest, and still appealing.
Use large, plain fonts and strong contrast, so older buyers can read.

say: And use only as much packaging as protection needs. If you reuse returned glass jars, check for chips and cracks, wash in hot soapy water, sterilise and dry fully before refilling.

say: Now prove it works. First record a baseline, your starting numbers, for at least four weeks with the old packaging. Then measure the same things for four weeks after.

card.title: Did the new pouch pay off?

say: With old nylon bags, Amaka sold 200 units at 500 naira. That is 100,000 naira. 12 were returned soft or torn, a damage rate of 6%.

card.title: Did the new pouch pay off?

say: With sealed pouches, she sold 240 units at 700 naira. That is 168,000 naira, and only 2 returns, about 0.8%.

card.title: Did the new pouch pay off?

say: The better packaging cost her 24,000 naira more. But after all costs, her profit went from about 30,000 to about 60,000 naira, and two shops now stock her.
She also notes that December demand might have helped. Be honest about other causes.

say: To remember. Complete your label and write dates clearly. Never fake a NAFDAC number. Make only claims you can prove. Measure before and after. And report honestly.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Every label item, dates as DD/MM/YYYY
Never print a NAFDAC number you do not have
Every claim true and provable; no cures
